To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the entropy change in the magneto-structural transition of metamagnetic Ni-Co-Mm-Ga alloys depends on both composition and atomic order.

(i) ΔS depends on the type of the magnetic order in both austenite and (ferro-) martensite phases; (ii) the magnetic entropy change in the metamagnetic transition is determined by the magnetic order in the austenite and the magnetic order in martensite is determined by the applied magnetic field; (iii) the atomic order degree is a crucial factor for the MT and its magnetic contribution.

the entropy change in the MT is strongly composition and atomic order dependant, and that both the magnetic and structural contributions to ΔS can be tuned by composition or thermal treatment, in such a manner that the MT can be induced by magnetic fields of different intensity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the transformation entropy and its magnetic contribution in Ni-Co-Mn- Ga alloys.
the determination and understanding of the behavior of the entropy change and magnetization jump in the metamagnetic Ni-Co-Man-Ga alloys as a function of the composition and thermal history.

the determination of the magnetic contribution to the MT entropy and the study of the factors that influence the MT in metamagnetic Ni-Co-Man-Ga shape memory alloys, in such a manner that the MT temperature can be adjusted to a desired value by composition and/or heat treatment.

the magnetic contribution to the entropy change in NiCoMnGa alloys is mainly related to the degree of magnetic order in the related phases.
